# Fieldnote Clinic Pilot: One-Page Summary

Fieldnote’s offline notes app was piloted from 1 September to 15 November in clinics in Pune, Nagpur, and Nashik. Nurses used shared tablets on home visits and synced notes at the clinic. The trial covered 412 visits: 168 in Pune, 139 in Nagpur, and 105 in Nashik.

## Results

The median sync time was 38 seconds. Nashik had the longest delays, reaching four minutes, as its Wi-Fi dropped several times a day. No notes were lost, and tablets lasted a full shift at every site. Nurses gave the app an average rating of 4.3/5. The visit template was the most valued feature, reducing write-up time from about nine minutes to five. Photo upload was the least liked feature because it was slow and confusing.

Two incidents occurred. On 22 September, two tablets editing the same offline visit created a duplicate patient record in Nagpur; staff merged it manually that day. On 14 October, an expired sync-server certificate caused a three-hour outage. Neither incident harmed a patient.

## Costs and clinic requests

The pilot spent ₹18.5 lakh of its ₹22 lakh budget: ₹9 lakh for tablets, ₹4 lakh for training, ₹3.5 lakh for support, and ₹2 lakh for the sync server. The remaining ₹3.5 lakh is reserved for the next phase.

Clinic leads requested simpler photo uploads, a warning when multiple tablets edit the same visit, and printed visit summaries for patients without phones. Nashik also requested queued syncing until Wi-Fi is stable.

## Recommendation

The team recommends expanding to 10 clinics in March, after simplifying photo upload and adding the simultaneous-edit warning. It also recommends monitoring certificate expiry going forward. A second review is planned for June.
